product.olivetti-m240.summary: The M24 evolution that combined greater speed with office, network and tax-adviser configurations.
product.olivetti-m240.history: Documented in Olivetti brochures dated September and November 1987, the M240 continued the M24 line as a compatible evolution for professional work. Olivetti offered it as a standalone workstation or a networked station, with word processing, spreadsheet and database applications. In Germany, the M240 Steuerberater configuration served tax advisers with DSSW/E software and a DATEV connection. Sources: brochures 04/112/PC/9.87 and 04/070/DVS/11.87.
product.olivetti-m240.warning: Historical sheet under research: BluMach contains two M240 implementations, still requiring comparison and validation for this sheet.
product.olivetti-m240.technical.variants: Expansion depends on the configuration. The general September 1987 brochure advertises seven 8-bit slots; the November Steuerberater brochure lists five, two 360 KB floppy drives, a 20 MB disk on a card and a second DATEV serial interface. Both figures are retained without assuming they describe the same equipment.
product.olivetti-m240.technical.cpu: The M240 accelerated its predecessor's design. The brochure and service guide document a 10 MHz 8086 and 640 KB with no wait states; the guide identifies BA200/BA208 boards and OMEGA 4 logic. An 8087 was offered as an option.
product.olivetti-m240.technical.video: The graphics card determines which monitor and modes can be used. The brochure offers OGC, with 640 × 400 monochrome graphics, and EGA-compatible OEC. The service guide adds the 8-bit VGA-compatible OVC GO729; this does not imply that all these options were sold from launch.
product.olivetti-m240.technical.ports: Switches adapt the machine to its peripherals. The guide, pp. 2-3/2-4, documents groups A/B and I/O ranges 060h–06Fh for the keyboard, 070h–07Fh for date and time, 378h–37Fh for parallel, 3F0h–3F7h for floppy and 3F8h–3FFh for serial.
product.olivetti-m240.technical.firmware: The BIOS revision matters when identifying each board. The guide's table on p. 2-1 associates 2.11 with PCHK (H) and PCHJ (L), and 2.12 with PCHL (H) and PCHM (L). 86Box documented a 2.11 dump in PR #4446. These are documentary references: this sheet does not certify the bytes of a local ROM.
product.olivetti-m240.technical.verified: The code has been reviewed without testing a boot. In BluMach 88f74ba3, m240 loads interleaved BIOS 2.12 and uses MM58274; olivetti_m240 loads a derived file identified as 2.11 and uses NVR_AT. The existence of both paths does not show that they are equivalent or validated.
product.olivetti-m240.technical.limitati: This sheet does not yet allow machine creation. The two paths need comparison, particularly the clock, configuration and resets, and a firmware set with provenance must be verified before validating boot. A publishable M240 image with clear rights is still pending.
product.olivetti-m240.technical.source_b: Olivetti, Personal Computer M240, Hardware-Informationen, 04/112/PC/9.87, three-page copy: M24 evolution, applications, CPU, memory, video and seven slots. Printed date checked.
product.olivetti-m240.technical.source_t: Olivetti, M240 Steuerberater, 04/070/DVS/11.87, three-page copy: tax-adviser configuration, DATEV, DSSW/E and five slots. Printed date checked.
product.olivetti-m240.technical.source_s: Olivetti, Personal Computer – Pocket Service Guide, M240 chapter, pp. 2-1–2-4: boards, BIOS revisions, video, switches and ports. Original preserved in the library's M24 record.
product.olivetti-m240.technical.source_c: BluMach 88f74ba3, m_xt_olivetti.c: m240 path, BIOS 2.12 and MM58274. Evidence of existing code, not physical validation.
product.olivetti-m240.technical.source_o: BluMach 88f74ba3, m_at_olivetti_m240.c: olivetti_m240 path, linear loading of the 2.11 derivative and NVR_AT. Its comments are not used as proof of the real hardware.
product.olivetti-m240.technical.source_8: 86Box, PR #4446, merged on 11 May 2024: report of the 2.11 dump and ROM-set update. It does not establish a local BluMach test.
